question.text: The IPEV Valuation Guidelines (December 2022) recommend that the best measure for valuing private equity portfolio companies from a Cat I/II AIF manager's perspective is:

answer.text: Historical cost with annual impairment testing
Fair value as defined under IND-AS 113 / IVS
Market capitalisation of listed comparables without adjustment

explanation.text: **The Logic:** The PDF Section 11.8.3 explicitly states the IPEV central theme: 'fair value is the best measure of valuing private equity portfolio companies.' Fair value per IND-AS 113 is 'the price that would be received to sell an asset in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.' This is the definition endorsed by the IPEV Board via its understanding with IVSC. **The Trap:** Historical cost ignores value changes; book value is a floor only; listed-cap without adjustment ignores DLOM. IPEV 2022 is explicit that FAIR VALUE (not cost, not book) is the gold standard. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same IPEV fair value principle. XIX-A (Distributor) tests whether reported NAV equals fair value for LP reporting. IND-AS 113 is tested in CA Final Financial Reporting paper. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Your PPM's valuation-methodology section must reference 'IPEV Guidelines 2022 and IVCA guidance note' by name. SEBI inspections of Cat I/II AIFs consistently ask for this disclosure.
